services.name: Float Fest 2025
services.desc: The Great Minnesotan Float Together! Come one, come all to the very first Float Fest — a celebration of community, river life, and summer joy on the mighty Mississippi! Paddle with us from Coon Rapids Dam to Boom Island for a day of fun, connection, and floating together. Choose Your Own Adventure Pick your put-in location based on your preferred distance: Coon Rapids Dam – ~9 miles Gateway Regional Park – ~9 miles River Park – ~8.5 miles North Mississippi Regional Park (Camden Boat Launch) – ~4.5 miles There are several Purchasing options. 1) $40.00 Registration for those who choose to BYOB

services.name: Float Fest 2026 - Presented by Bolton & Menk - North Mississippi
Paddle Share: Nature Route
services.desc: Start just downstream of the Coon Rapids Dam. Paddle along this quiet, winding stretch of the Mississippi River. Towering tree canopy drapes over the riverbank, providing habitat for bald eagles and migratory birds. There are many undeveloped islands along the route. Paddle through the backwaters to see spiny soft-shelled turtles sunning themselves on logs and driftwood. Keep an eye out for egrets, wild turkeys, turkey vultures, otters, geese, deer, and fox. You may also encounter dragonflies and other insect life landing to rest on your kayak as you relax and enjoy the natural outdoor show. Nature Route 7.5 Miles ~ 2 hours 30

services.name: Paddle Share: City Route
services.desc: Launch from the sandy beach at North Mississippi Regional Park. Enjoy the scenic treelined riverbank and watch as industry and development begin to appear downstream. Paddle past the Upper Harbor Terminal, a site the City of Minneapolis plans to redevelop. Explore the islands that serve as a heron rookery and hear the raucous calls as the birds nest and raise their chicks. Pass under the Lowry Avenue bridge and enjoy the best view of the Minneapolis 4 Miles. 1 hour 15 minutes

services.name: Paddle Share: Nature to City Route
services.desc: This is the longest Paddle Share adventure! It will sweep you from peaceful nature, past industrial structures along the riverfront in North Minneapolis, all the way to stunning views of the city skyline at Boom Island park. This route features the opportunity enjoy the treelined riverbanks. Keep an eye out for egrets, wild turkeys, turkey vultures, otters, geese, deer, and fox. See the industrial shoreline from a different perspective and enjoy the cityscape of downtown Minneapolis as you finish your paddle. There is plenty of time to stop along the way, paddle around islands, and take in 8.5 Miles ~3 hours

services.name: Paddle Share: Pickerel
services.desc: Pickerel Lake is located in Lilydale Regional Park, a park along the Mississippi River near downtown Saint Paul. The lake is surrounded by floodplain forest and scenic bluffs. There is an abundance of fish in the lake and in mid-summer lily pads dot the surface. Look for the eagle’s nest near the powerlines, and the river otters that hang out along the forest shoreline across the Fish, paddle, or birdwatch on this rich oxbow lake!

services.name: Paddle Share: Gorge Route
services.desc: This new route brings paddlers through the only true gorge on the Mississippi River. This calm stretch was formed thousands of years ago, when a cascading waterfall slowly making its way upriver carved out a deep channel. The route begins at Bohemian Flats Park, north of the University of Minnesota west bank campus, and ends at the Minneapolis Rowing Club, just north of Lake Street Bridge. To complete the trip, refuel at a nearby restaurant or coffee shop, like the Longfellow Grill, Dairy Queen, The Bungalow Club, Hi-Lo Diner, Dogwood Coffee or El 3 Miles ~1hour
